pr_title: Fix selection being deleted and indentation not being accounted for. Fixes #55855
pr_body:
This fixes the editor deleting the selected text when creating a new line below or above the current one with Ctrl + Enter. I've also made a small edit that will make sure that the indentation is properly accounted for, as if you were creating a new line from the end of the line (i.e, the ':' will be properly accounted for).

Here is a demonstration of how this works after the commit:

![4FYN5OA91Q](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2719468/145731746-91f1b070-9ebf-4cd1-b535-cdc6df8f978b.gif)

Fixes #55855

issue_context.title: Ctrl + Enter replaces selected text with a newline in the script editor (should move to the next line instead)
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v3.4.stable.official [206ba70f4] and the online editor: https://editor.godotengine.org/releases/3.4.1.rc2/

### System information

Windows 10 21H1, Geforce GTX 550 Ti, GLES2 and GLES3

### Issue description

In the script editor.
Selecting text and pressing `ctrl enter` or `shift ctrl enter`,
replaces the selection with a newline.

Expected:
Cancel the selection and move the cursor to a:
- new empty line below (`ctrl enter`)
- new empty line above (`shift ctrl enter`)

This would make `ctrl (shift) enter` behave the same with or without selected text.

If the intention is to replace the selected text with a new line,
then `enter` can be pressed without holding down a modifier key.


### Steps to reproduce

- create a new or open an existing script
- type some text, for example:
```
var test = 3
```
- select `test`

>Explanation of symbols:
cursor = `|` (vertical bar)
selection start = `[`
selection end = `]`

```
var [test]| = 3
```
- press `ctrl enter`

### observed
```
var 
| = 3
```
Result: A newline replaced the selected text.

### expected:
After `ctrl enter`:
```
var test = 3
|
```
Result: The cursor is on a new empty line below, and the selected text stays unmodified.

Or after pressing `shift ctrl enter`:
```
|
var test = 3
```
Result:  The cursor is on a new empty line above, and the selected text stays unmodified.


### notes:
An application that shows the expected behavior is Visual Studio Code.

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
